# “At the Feet of the Guru”— Studying the New SRF Lessons
### 2020 SRF Online World Convocation

## Opening Prayer

*O Divine Mother, Heavenly Father, Friend, Beloved God,*
*Great Gurus of Self-Realization Fellowship—Jesus Christ, Bhagavan Krishna, Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Sri Yukteswar, and our beloved Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda—*
*Saints and sages of all religions, we bow to you all.*

*Divine Beloved, open our hearts and minds to receive the sacred vibrations of Thy direct guidance. As we study these holy teachings, may we realize that we are not merely reading words on a page, but are sitting at the feet of the Guru, bathed in his wisdom, his unconditional love, and his transforming grace. Grant us the dedication, the concentration, and the deep devotion to practice these teachings daily, that we may realize our oneness with Thee. Om. Shanti. Shanti. Shanti.*

***

## Welcome to the Sacred Sanctuary of the Soul

My dear spiritual family, what a joy and a privilege it is to welcome all of you, from every corner of this world, to this sacred class of the 2020 Self-Realization Fellowship Online World Convocation. Though we may be physically separated by vast oceans and continents, we are gathered here as one global family, united in the eternal, omnipresent love of our beloved Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda.

Our subject today is one that lies at the very heart of the disciple’s journey: **“At the Feet of the Guru”— Studying the New SRF Lessons**. 

In the ancient spiritual tradition of India, the word *Upanishad* literally means "sitting down near"—sitting at the feet of the illuminated master to receive the sacred, whisper-soft truths of the soul. When we sit with our Lessons, we are doing exactly that. We are entering a private, holy sanctuary where the guru speaks directly to our souls. We are sitting at the feet of Paramahansa Yogananda.

Many of you have recently received, or are currently studying, the new edition of the *Self-Realization Fellowship Lessons*. This monumental release, which our beloved past presidents Sri Daya Mata and Sri Mrinalini Mata labored over for decades under Gurudeva's direct guidance, is a divine dispensation for the modern age. These lessons are not just an intellectual course in philosophy. They are a systematic, step-by-step practical guide to direct personal experience of the Divine.

***

## The Living Presence in the Lessons

Our Guru often told his disciples, *"When I am gone, the Lessons will be the Guru."* He explained that he had poured his very life-force, his spiritual realization, and his love into these writings. 

**Story • The Musk Deer’s Search**

Story: Gurudeva often used the beautiful classic analogy of the musk deer to describe the spiritual search of humanity. Deep in the forests of the Himalayas, the musk deer runs frantically hither and thither, searching for the source of an exquisite, intoxicating scent that fills the air. It climbs dangerous cliffs, tears through thorny bushes, and wears itself out in a desperate, external search. Finally, exhausted and near death, the deer collapses. As its nose bends down toward its own chest, it realizes that the source of the fragrant scent was never outside; it was emanating from its own navel all along. In the same way, we wander through the wilderness of material life, seeking joy, love, and peace in outer relationships, possessions, and accomplishments. But the source of that peace is within us. The SRF Lessons are the map that guides us back to our own center, where the fragrance of Divine Joy eternally dwells.

To study these lessons is to engage in a sacred covenant. When you read the words of the Guru with deep concentration, you are not engaging in passive reading. You are practicing *Svadhyaya*—sacred study that leads to communion. Each sentence contains a seed of high spiritual vibration. If you approach them with the right attitude, those seeds will take root in the fertile soil of your consciousness and transform your entire life.

***

## Practical Guidelines for Studying the New Lessons

To receive the maximum benefit from the New SRF Lessons, we must learn *how* to study them. Let us explore some essential, practical guidelines that will help you establish a deep, meditative connection with these teachings.

### 1. Create a Sacred Space and Time

Do not read the Lessons as you would read a daily newspaper, a novel, or a textbook on your commute. Treat them with the utmost reverence. 
* Choose a quiet, clean environment, preferably in your meditation room or before your altar.
* Light a candle or incense, and gaze at the pictures of our line of Gurus.
* Dedicate a specific, uninterrupted block of time each week—such as a quiet morning or evening—to study a new Lesson.

By establishing this physical and mental boundary, you signal to your subconscious and superconscious minds that you are entering a sacred space of divine instruction.

### 2. Begin with Prayer and Attunement

Before you open a Lesson, close your eyes and offer a deep prayer to God and Gurudeva. Ask for the receptive capacity to understand not just the intellectual meaning of the words, but the spiritual essence behind them. 

Remember, the Guru's consciousness is omnipresent. When you call upon him with sincerity, his spirit hovers over you, illuminating your understanding. 

### 3. Read with "Devotional Intelligence"

Read slowly. If a paragraph strikes a chord deep within your heart, stop. Close your eyes. Meditate on that truth. Let it sink deep into your subconscious. 

**Story • Sri Yukteswar's Counsel on Digestion**

Story: Our great Paramguru, Swami Sri Yukteswarji, was known for his rigorous training of his disciples. He once observed a student who was reading spiritual scriptures day and night, boasting about how many holy books he had completed. Sri Yukteswar looked at him gently and said, "It is not how much food you put into your stomach that nourishes you, but how much you digest. In the same way, it is not how many books you read that elevates your consciousness, but how many of their truths you assimilate and live in your daily life." Gurudeva took this lesson to heart, and it is the very foundation of the SRF Lessons. They are structured to be received week by week, allowing us the time to digest, practice, and live one truth before moving on to the next.

Do not rush through the Lessons. The new edition is beautifully designed with summary points, highlighted quotes, and practical application sections. Use these features to check your understanding and to keep your study active and engaged.

***

## The Science of Yoga: Integrating Theory and Practice

The unique glory of the SRF Lessons is that they combine the highest spiritual philosophy with scientific techniques of meditation. They are not dry doctrines; they are an experimental science of the soul.

In these Lessons, you are taught the three great pillars of the SRF path:
1. **The Energization Exercises:** Which teach you how to draw cosmic energy directly into the body through the medulla oblongata, recharging every cell with vitality and health.
2. **The Hong-Sau Technique of Concentration:** Which quietens the breath, calms the restless mind, and focuses your attention inward.
3. **The Aum Technique of Meditation:** Which expands your consciousness beyond the limits of the physical body, allowing you to hear and merge with the creative vibration of the universe.

These techniques are not separate from the study of the Lessons; they are the practical applications of the truths you read. When you practice these techniques with precision and devotion, you cultivate the quiet, receptive mind that is necessary to truly comprehend the deep spiritual mysteries presented in the text.

***

## Cultivating a Relationship with the Guru

For many seekers, the question arises: *"How can I feel close to a Guru who is no longer physically present on this earth?"*

The answer lies in the spiritual law of attunement. The Guru is not the physical body; the Guru is the infinite consciousness of God expressing through a channel of divine love. The physical body may pass away, but the Guru's love, his guidance, and his active interest in your spiritual welfare are eternal.

**Story • The Whispering Presence**

Story: A disciple of Gurudeva once shared a deeply moving experience that occurred many years after the Master had entered mahasamadhi. This disciple was going through a period of intense spiritual dry spell and doubt. One night, feeling lonely and disconnected, they sat at their altar and opened one of the SRF Lessons that they had read many times before. As they began to read, they decided to read the words aloud, imagining that Gurudeva was speaking them directly. Suddenly, the room was filled with a tangible, sweet aroma of roses—a scent often associated with Gurudeva’s presence. The disciple felt a wave of divine peace wash over their heart, and a quiet, inner voice whispered, "I am here. I have never left you. The words you hold in your hands are my living voice." From that moment on, the disciple’s doubts vanished, replaced by an unshakable conviction that the Guru is forever present in his teachings.

Every time you open your Lessons with love and devotion, you are tuning your mental radio to the exact frequency of the Guru’s consciousness. You will find that answers to your deepest personal problems will suddenly jump out from the pages of a Lesson you are reading. You will find that the strength to face a difficult trial is silently infused into your heart while you study. This is the living power of the Guru-disciple relationship.

***

## Commitment to the Path

As you embark on or continue your study of these New Lessons, remember that consistency is the key to spiritual success. Spiritual progress does not come from occasional, frantic efforts, but from steady, daily, loving application.

Make a commitment to yourself and to Gurudeva:
* I will study my Lesson regularly.
* I will practice the techniques of meditation daily with devotion.
* I will strive to apply the practical psychological and spiritual principles in my daily life—in my family, my workplace, and my inner world.

By doing so, you will find your life changing in beautiful, subtle ways. You will find a deep, underlying peace that remains undisturbed by the storms of the world. You will find a spontaneous joy bubbling up from your heart for no external reason. You will find yourself growing in love, patience, and understanding toward all souls.

***

## Conclusion and Blessing

Beloved friends, we are living in a time of great global change and uncertainty. The world is searching for stability, for peace, and for truth. The timeless teachings of Kriya Yoga, brought to the West by our beloved Gurudeva, are the anchor we need to navigate these turbulent times.

Let us hold fast to this anchor. Let us sit daily at the feet of the Guru through the study of his Lessons and the practice of his techniques. Let us become living examples of his teachings—beacons of light, love, and joy in a world that sorely needs them.

May the blessing of Paramahansa Yogananda, and of all the Great Gurus, rest upon you, guide you, and lead you to the ultimate harbor of Divine Freedom.

*Jai Guru!*
